diagnostic_evidence.quote: These, together with the $n_1n_2\ldots n_NN$ divisions needed to compute $\Y$,
we need one division, $(n_1 - i_1) + (n_2 - i_2) + \ldots + (n_N - i_N)$ products in the numerator

issues.failure_explanation: With P = n_1...n_N and S = sum_j n_j, the paper's own displayed addends are (P/2)[5S - N] multiplications, (P/2)[5S - 3N - 2] additions/subtractions, and PN divisions; these sum to P[5S - N - 1], not the printed P[5S - N + 1] (off by 2P). Moreover the PN divisions figure contradicts the paper's own per-entry count of one division per entry of Y (one quotient in (10)), under which the correct total is P[5S - 2N]. The printed equality is false under every consistent reading; only lower-order terms are affected, and the leading term 5P*S (about 5Nn^{N+1} for n_j = n) and the O(n^{N+1}) conclusion survive.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the tally with one division per entry: the method costs n_1...n_N[5*sum_j n_j - 2N] flops excluding the Schur decompositions; a local recomputation of the displayed sums with no other change.
issues.overall_effect: The exact floating-point-operation tally advertised for the method (excluding Schur decompositions) is incorrect in its lower-order terms, and the total division count is inflated by a factor N. The asymptotic cost, the algorithms, and all numerical claims are unaffected.
issues.title: Final flop-count formula does not follow from the paper's own displayed addends
issues.why_classification: A short local recomputation of displayed sums fixes it; the leading-order cost, the O(n^{N+1}) claim, the algorithms, and all advertised guarantees survive unchanged, so there is no mathematical loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: & u_t(\xx, t) = \Delta u(\xx, t) + 2\xx\cdot\nabla u(\xx, t) + (2N+1)u(\xx, t) - \exp(-\xx\cdot\xx), & & \xx\in\mathbb R^N, t > 0,

issues.failure_explanation: For u = c(t)exp(-|x|^2) the spatial operator gives Delta u + 2x.curl-grad u + (2N+1)u = c(t)exp(-|x|^2), since the second directional derivatives sum to (4|x|^2 - 2N)e^{-|x|^2} and 2x.cgrad e^{-|x|^2} = -4|x|^2 e^{-|x|^2}; with the forcing -exp(-x.x) the PDE reduces to c'(t) = c(t) - 1. The claimed solution c = 1 + e^t satisfies this ODE but gives u(x,0) = 2exp(-|x|^2), whereas the stated initial condition requires u(x,0) = exp(-x.x), i.e. c(0) = 1. The stated initial value problem therefore has the stationary solution u(x,t) = exp(-|x|^2), not the claimed time-dependent one; the initial value problem as printed and the claimed exact solution are incompatible, so the reported error 9.6811e-14 at t = 1, measured against the claimed solution, is not supported as written.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the solution of \eqref{e:uxt} is $u(\xx, t) = (1+\exp(t))\exp(-\xx\cdot\xx)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct one of the two inconsistent items: either state the initial condition as u(xx,0) = 2exp(-xx.xx), in which case the claimed exact solution (1+exp(t))exp(-xx.xx) is correct, or state the exact solution as the stationary exp(-xx.xx); either is a one-line local correction restoring consistency of the benchmark.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical validation of the advertised advection-diffusion application in Section 5.2 (error 9.6811e-14 at t = 1, N = 6, against the stated exact solution) becomes unreliable, and the abstract's claim of accurately computing the solution of an advection-diffusion equation on R^N inherits the inconsistency; the method itself (Algorithm alg:sylvesterND, Theorem theo:evolND) is unaffected.
issues.title: Stated exact solution of the advection-diffusion problem does not satisfy the stated initial condition
issues.why_classification: Either one-token correction (initial condition or stated solution) restores full consistency; the method, its cost analysis, and the advertised accuracy claims all survive unchanged, so no substantive mathematical content is lost.
